## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Amarādevīpañhajātaka* (Ja 112), also titled *Amarādevīpañha*, is a short entry within the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral]. The text opens with the verse line *Yena sattubilangā cā* ("Cakes and gruel") [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral]. Rather than presenting an extended narrative in place, the traditional commentary indicates that this riddle or narrative concerning Queen Amarā will appear fully in the *Ummaggajātaka* (*Ayam Amarādevīpañho nāma tatth' eva avibhavissati*) [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral lists four translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral]. In text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus records two matching Pali passages shared with the sixth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Chaṭṭho bhāgo), spanning segments §0.4–1.6 of this text and §2549_9–2552 of the commentary (with a similarity score of 0.93), while no cross-language matches meet the threshold [DharmaNexus].
